summary: Claude / GPT / Gemini / Grok through a GitHub Copilot seat. Public endpoint by default; a GitHub Enterprise Cloud data-residency tenant is supported as an alternative.

requires.name: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN
requires.description: A Copilot OAuth access token (gho_...). PI sends it straight through as the API key; there is no token exchange on this path.
requires.howTo: Reuse the token an existing OAuth client already holds (VS Code / another editor integration), or run `/login github-copilot` ONCE in PI on a public seat and copy the value out of ~/.pi/agent/auth.json. Put it in ~/.pi/secrets.env as COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=gho_... (chmod 600).

requires.name: PI_COPILOT_QUOTA_TOKEN
requires.description: Optional classic ghp_ PAT used only by the quota meter extension. Never used for chat.
requires.howTo: github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens (classic). A fine-grained github_pat_... token is rejected: the premium-usage endpoint does not accept one.

prompts.label: Which Copilot endpoint does your seat use?

choices.label: Public github.com Copilot (api.githubcopilot.com) - the normal answer
GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (copilot-api.<tenant>.ghe.com)

prompts.label: Your GHE data-residency tenant slug
prompts.help: Only the slug. For an enterprise reachable at https://<tenant>.ghe.com, the Copilot API host is copilot-api.<tenant>.ghe.com.

validate.message: lowercase tenant slug only - no scheme, no dots, no trailing slash

notes: WHY modelOverrides EXISTS AT ALL. PI's bundled Copilot catalogue declares a 1 000 000 (and for some ids 1 050 000) token context window for models whose Copilot endpoint serves far less. PI's compaction threshold is `contextWindow - reserveTokens`, so an over-declared window makes compaction fire far too late: the request is already larger than the endpoint accepts, and the turn dies (or is silently truncated upstream) instead of compacting. The rule this file follows is: a declared window is min(200000, what the endpoint actually serves).

THE VALUES ABOVE WERE MEASURED ON ONE TENANT. They are deliberately conservative - under-declaring only makes compaction fire earlier, which is safe; over-declaring is what breaks. Re-measure on yours and edit config/models.json (or this fragment and re-run the installer) if you need the extra room.

HOW TO RE-MEASURE. Send a request whose prompt is a known token count and grow it until the endpoint returns a context-length error; the largest size that still succeeds is the real window. `pi --list-models` shows what PI currently believes. Do not raise a number you have not observed.

NEVER RUN `/login github-copilot` WITH THIS FRAGMENT. PI's Copilot provider registers two auth methods. The apiKey method sends COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN straight through and leaves the `baseUrl` above intact. The OAuth method's resolver ALWAYS returns its own baseUrl (derived from the token's proxy-ep hint), and at request time `applyAuth()` does `auth.baseUrl ? {...model, baseUrl: auth.baseUrl} : model` - so an OAuth credential silently overrides the baseUrl written here. On the public endpoint that is harmless; on an enterprise data-residency tenant it sends your traffic somewhere else.

THE `apiKey` FIELD IS NOT OPTIONAL. A github-copilot block with no `apiKey` key at all is read as unconfigured and PI drops the ENTIRE built-in Copilot catalogue from /model, Ctrl+P and every tier that names a github-copilot/* id. That is a stronger failure than a present-but-empty reference (which leaves the models listed and fails at request time). Measured, not theorised.
DO NOT SET `api`. Copilot dispatches three different wire APIs per model; PI picks the right one from its own catalogue.

MODEL LIST IS UNFILTERED ON THE apiKey PATH. PI narrows the catalogue to the credential's entitlement only for OAuth credentials, so /model lists every model in the bundled catalogue regardless of what your seat actually grants. A 403/404 on a specific id is account policy surfacing through an unfiltered list, not a bug. Some seats also require enabling a model once in the editor's model picker before the API accepts it.
NEVER TOUCH THE X-Initiator HEADER. GitHub's meter keys premium-request counting on it. `bin/pi-check` rule PC-15 fails the build if any extension references it.

verify.label: the endpoint answers with your token
